title: Dynamic Causal Structure Discovery and Causal Effect Estimation

problem.claim: Causal structure learning seeks to learn hidden causal relationships among variables represented by a directed acyclic graph.

gap.claim: Many existing approaches assume causal relationships remain unchanged over time, an assumption that may not hold in real life.

contributions.claim: A framework models dynamic causal graphs whose causal relations can vary over time.
A basis approximation method is incorporated into score-based causal discovery to capture dynamic graph patterns.
An autoregressive structure captures contemporaneous and time-lagged causal relationships while allowing them to vary over time.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their framework for time-varying causal relations as new.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The proposed algorithm provides past-time estimates and future-time predictions of causal graphs.
Simulations were conducted to demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed method.
A COVID-data analysis examines how the effect of policy restrictions changes.

narrative_sequence.summary: Causal relationships are commonly represented with directed acyclic graphs, and deep-learning approaches learn hidden causal structures.
Existing approaches commonly assume causal relationships are stable over time.
The paper introduces a time-varying causal-graph framework using basis approximation and an autoregressive structure.
The method is used for past estimation and future prediction, simulations, and COVID policy-effect analysis.

unknowns: No datasets, simulation settings, baselines, quantitative results, or uncertainty estimates are specified.
The abstract does not describe the algorithm's computational requirements or assumptions beyond time-varying causal relations.
